analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side CHANGELOG.md excerpts (lines 1867-2358) in a region the file_changes map does not mark as changed. The changed hunk is head lines 11-25 at the top of the file, which is only visible as a truncated patch excerpt. This is documentation only, with no executable code, authorization logic, cryptography, or configuration change.

The visible patch text relabels the v0.10.2 candidate as v0.10.3 and describes an MLX submodule pin change (libs/mlx-swift eedca444 to 4926d3d9; libs/mlx and nested mlx ff4bb35b to 31f550af) that fixes an M5 Metal kernel compile crash. That change is a dependency bump in the native inference runtime (TB-007), and it is not visible in the supplied evidence. The submodule diff and the MLX kernel argument correction cannot be reviewed here. The next pass should inspect the submodule pin changes. They touch the inference engine and the attention kernels, which could affect numerical behavior and the KV/prefix-cache identity bindings (T-041), so their effect on the checkpoint identity needs checking.

The changelog also says the KV-backend guard binds only the tripping version and clears on upgrade. Neither the guard implementation nor the watchdog and auto-update behavior is supplied (T-043, which is about the watchdog being the same replaceable binary). The text states that the guard clears on 0.10.3, which is a documented behavior claim, not a verified control change.

The base excerpts I examined contain historical release notes only. I found no secrets and no instructions in them. I found no concrete security regression or invalidated threat-model assumption in the supplied evidence. The remaining uncertainty is the unseen submodule and runtime change, so I am flagging deeper review for the code diffs.
